verdict: OK to lend in Saharanpur sugar & ethanol — back the surviving mills and their cane suppliers, not the closed-mill ecosystem.
title: Saharanpur Sugar & Ethanol: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A mill buys cane from farmers within a 15-25 km catchment, crushes it for 4-5 months, and sells sugar, molasses and ethanol.** Cash comes in through the year but cane payment goes out during the crush, so the working-capital cycle is the whole credit story. The DM's instruction at Sarsawa that cane dues be paid on time and weighing be transparent tells you the state is watching payment discipline [1]. **So when a proposal lands, check the mill's cane-payment arrears position first; if arrears are running beyond the season, ask for the payment schedule and the DM's correspondence.**

## What has changed in Saharanpur now
**Two mills in the district have shut — Shakumbhari and Daya — and their cane centres have been reallocated to other mills [3].** Sarsawa has opened its 2026-27 crush [1] and Nanauta starts 1 November [2]. That reallocation is the growth signal: surviving mills get more cane without buying more land. **Pursue the mills absorbing reallocated centres and the larger cane suppliers feeding them; avoid anyone whose business depended on Shakumbhari or Daya procurement.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in recovery rate and in ethanol, not in sugar alone.** ICRA notes remunerative ethanol prices and interest subvention on distillery capex help prevent cane arrears piling up, and that ethanol plus firm domestic prices offset cyclicality for integrated mills [10]. A refining capex of about Rs 70 crore improved realisations by roughly Rs 0.5-1.0/kg at one rated mill [9]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower is integrated into ethanol or refining; if it is pure raw-sugar, ask what protects it in a low-recovery year.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the crush, not the calendar.** Peer results show the cycle is live: Triveni's Q1 FY27 saw improved profitability and reduced debt on strong sugar and distillery margins despite lower cane yields [5], and EID Parry's average realisation rose to INR 51.2 per kilogram from INR 43.7 [6]. **Take monthly: cane crushed, recovery rate, sugar and ethanol realisations, cane arrears, and stock statements; if recovery falls below the prior season, ask for the yield data before renewing limits.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch cane arrears and centre allocation.** If a mill's reallocated centres are withdrawn or cane supply slips, the crush shortens and fixed costs bite. Rating commentary flags profitability as vulnerable to agro-climatic risk and industry cyclicality [10]. **If arrears cross one season or the mill misses a cane payment date, move the account to review and ask for a fresh CMA before any enhancement.**

## The data call
**The data pack scores Saharanpur sugar at 76 — above the 65 lend line [D].** UP GST collections grew 14.2% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], a local tailwind, though UP electricity demand grew 8.6% against India's 9.5% [D]. **Lend to integrated, cane-secured mills and their large suppliers; decline the closed-mill supplier chain.**
